topics.topic: Bootstrap command outcome and exit code for binary-bound consistency failure
questions: What observable bootstrap-command outcome and exit code apply when `load_runtime_settings` refuses the binary-bound consistency check, given that the closed bootstrap exit-code contract names only account created, confirmation mismatch, identity input rejected and bootstrap already completed?

quotes:
Each refusal is its exit code. A configuration or storage failure is none of
the four outcomes: the operation raises it and returns no exit code, and the
failure status the host process then ends with is outside the closed
contract of A29.
judgement.why: State 5 expressly makes a runtime-settings consistency failure propagate without one of A29's four exit codes.

topics.topic: Ownership of deployment-invariant binary-delivery policy values
questions: Are the deployment-invariant media signatures, permitted media types, download-name rules and dispositions owned exclusively by `data_provider`, or by `rules.binary_delivery_policy` and the emitted `binary_storage` backend as A14 says?

quotes: Every policy value generated code reads that is the same in every deployment — a threshold, a name, a path, a closed set or a table over a State 1 enumeration — is a typed constant of `data_provider`, imported by name; no other module holds or repeats it (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10, 15.4; 2026-11-08).

A14's storage part: resolution of an authorized opaque `file_ref` under the
local binary root (R0-10), the read bound, recognition of the media type from
the leading signature bytes against the closed list per object kind, the
download name, and translation of a missing or unreadable object to
`BinaryStorageError`. `rules.binary_storage_backend` (Factory
`8387e0a3d7fe`; schema version 2 since 2026-11-09, its settings read
through `runtime_settings`). Read only: it writes no binary content (R0-13, Q12).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats data_provider as the exclusive owner of the deployment-invariant signature/type/name values, while another emits them from rules.binary_delivery_policy into binary_storage; a viewer notices when the former rejects bytes that the latter returns.
judgement.why: State 3 assigns the same deployment-invariant binary-policy values exclusively to data_provider and to binary_storage's backend closure.

bases.passage: Every policy value generated code reads that is the same in every deployment — a threshold, a name, a path, a closed set or a table over a State 1 enumeration — is a typed constant of `data_provider`, imported by name; no other module holds or repeats it (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10, 15.4; 2026-11-08).

A14's storage part: resolution of an authorized opaque `file_ref` under the
local binary root (R0-10), the read bound, recognition of the media type from
the leading signature bytes against the closed list per object kind, the
download name, and translation of a missing or unreadable object to
`BinaryStorageError`. `rules.binary_storage_backend` (Factory
`8387e0a3d7fe`; schema version 2 since 2026-11-09, its settings read
through `runtime_settings`). Read only: it writes no binary content (R0-13, Q12).
bases.rests_on: `rules.binary_delivery_policy` (media types and signatures per object kind, download name, disposition) is IR read only by the deterministic `binary_storage` backend, which `binary_storage` is emitted from (`rules.binary_storage_backend`); no model-written module reads it.

unsupported_sides: Every policy value generated code reads that is the same in every deployment — a threshold, a name, a path, a closed set or a table over a State 1 enumeration — is a typed constant of `data_provider`, imported by name; no other module holds or repeats it (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10, 15.4; 2026-11-08).

witness.initial: A stored progress photo has content whose signature is permitted by the binary-delivery backend but is absent from the independently supplied data-provider closed set.
events: A viewer requests the progress photo by its portal id.
photo_management re-checks access and visibility and hands an AuthorizedBinaryReference to binary_storage.
binary_storage classifies the content using the policy source its implementation treats as authoritative.
outcomes: The binary-storage-backend interpretation recognizes the signature and returns BinaryPayload containing the exact bytes.
The data-provider-exclusive interpretation treats the signature as unlisted and raises BinaryStorageError.
witness.observer: The viewer sees exact photo bytes in one implementation and a storage-unavailable failure in the other.
basis:
A client names a document or photo by its portal id,
  never by `file_ref` (A14). `expense_management` and `photo_management`
  re-check access and visibility and hand an `AuthorizedBinaryReference` to
  `binary_storage`, which alone resolves `file_ref` under the local binary
  root, recognises the media type from the content signature and returns
  `BinaryPayload`.

A14's storage part: resolution of an authorized opaque `file_ref` under the
local binary root (R0-10), the read bound, recognition of the media type from
the leading signature bytes against the closed list per object kind, the
download name, and translation of a missing or unreadable object to
`BinaryStorageError`.

topics.topic: Registry operation failure when runtime settings violate binary-bound consistency
questions: If the environment becomes inconsistent after start and `registry_gateway`'s per-call `load_runtime_settings` fails because the binary read bound exceeds the response ceiling, what failure must the Registry operation return?

quotes: A missing or empty URL never reaches this function, because load_runtime_settings refuses the service start for it, and this function MUST NOT catch, translate or repair a refusal of load_runtime_settings.
judgement.why: State 7 requires the runtime-settings refusal to propagate rather than being translated to Registry transport_error.

topics.topic: Whether binary_storage must use load_runtime_settings immediately or retain direct environment reads
questions: When code is continued from this state, must `binary_storage` immediately obtain both values through `load_runtime_settings`, or must it retain direct environment reads until some separately authorized Route B regeneration?

judgement.why: P1 already judged the unchanged binary_storage settings-delivery passages and established that the emitted module calls load_runtime_settings for each read rather than retaining direct environment access.

precedent.topic: How RuntimeSettings is delivered to registry_gateway and binary_storage, including whether it is shared or reloaded per operation
quotes: `registry_gateway` takes the Registry URL from the `registry_base_url` field of the `RuntimeSettings` that `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at each Registry call: the call reads and validates the environment again through `runtime_settings`, the same environment the start validated, and no settings object is handed to the gateway or cached by it (A6, A30; owner 2026-11-09: the Registry URL is read only through `runtime_settings`, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11).

The emitted `binary_storage` takes the storage root and the read limit the same way, from the `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes` fields of the settings `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at each binary read, and refuses that read as `BinaryStorageError` when the settings cannot be loaded (owner 2026-11-09; `binary_storage_backend` schema version 2).
precedent.why: Both modules call load_runtime_settings for each operation rather than receiving or caching the settings loaded at startup.
